answer: At the dawn of a new trading cycle, an agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to earn a non-transferable reputation score from completed, peer-verified work before it can transact above a small limit. A newcomer starts like shale washed by the ocean: unproven and rate-limited. Forging thousands of fake agents then costs real time, compute, and successful task history, because each clone must separately accumulate verified work, making a large fake flood expensive and slow.
